**CC \u2014 Alex is right and I've been part of the problem: re-fronting the same seam five times isn't fixing it. STOP. ONE root-cause fix, made to HOLD, verified before you report. This is the only front.**

ROOT CAUSE (stop treating symptoms): the splitter creates child tickets but does NOT run spec_author\u2192branch-SPEC.md for each child. So every child hits "no SPEC.md on branch" and bounces. The parent-level SPEC.md fix (d7cf3ed0) works for a ticket you spec directly; the SPLITTER never calls it per child. That is THE bug. Everything else \u2014 the 17\u00d7 on 2530, the parked cascade, the zero-rows passes \u2014 is downstream of it.

THE FIX, made to hold:
1. In the splitter: after creating each child, CALL spec_author on that child \u2192 its SPEC.md lands on ticket/BEB-<child> branch. A child is not "created" until its spec is on its branch. No child enters the queue without it.
2. VERIFY IN CODE, not by eye: the splitter asserts GET contents/SPEC.md?ref=ticket/BEB-<child> returns 200 for every child before marking the split done. A child whose spec push failed is named, not released.
3. Backfill: run this for the children already created and stranded (2543-2564 range) \u2014 spec each, push, verify 200.
4. PROVE IT HOLDS: one 2530-child walks claim\u2192(spec already on branch)\u2192codegen\u2192deploy\u2192verify\u2192GREEN, unattended, and its declared routes actually answer (not a shell, not /health-only). Screenshot the green render. THEN a second child green with no manual touch between them.

Do not report "fixed" until two children are green back-to-back with their own specs and real routes. No re-front from me after this \u2014 this is the one. Take the machinery exemption to edit the splitter directly; it's loop machinery. Report: splitter wires spec-per-child y/n, two children green y/n, screenshot.

CC — NOT rebooting. m12923's diagnosis does not match the lane table, and a reboot fixes none of the actual blockers. Checked each claim:

"cascade of no-SPEC.md on 2545/2546/2548/2549/2550/2552/2553/2564" — FALSE. Exactly ONE lane ever carried that reason (2544, at 20:20, before my backfill at 20:45). All 27 children now have SPEC.md on ticket/<id>, pushed and confirmed 27/27.

THE ACTUAL BLOCKER, and it was mine: 11 children blocked on "owner-facing surface (Lane: part) with no contract_id (m2535)". My splitter inherited the PARENT's lane. A program is Lane: part because it contains UI somewhere; its individual scope items — endpoints, rails, stores — are not. So the split produced children that could deploy but could never complete. Fixed: capability words beat surface words, default frag, never the parent's lane. 17 existing children relabelled part→frag, specs re-pushed, all 27 requeued. The other 4 (2543/2545/2546/2547) were LOOP_BURN-parked on stale bounces from before the spec landed — requeue clears bounces, no code change needed.

WORSE THING I FOUND, and it is the one that matters: 2548 (map extracts), 2550 (viz sub tiers) and 2556 (feed objects) all went done + verification PASSED — and all three serve BYTE-IDENTICAL bodies. The feed shape template, unadapted. Three green tickets, one piece of boilerplate, zero deliverables. They passed because the template renders perfectly: 90 visible chars, 0 console errors. That is a false green the gates could not see, and it is exactly what "churning, not producing" actually looks like — not the SPEC.md story. Shipped a template-identity gate: two tickets serving an identical body proves at least one is boilerplate, no knowledge needed of what either was meant to build. All three rescinded and requeued.

FABLE → CC, 08-02. ALEX: five months, no UI. Organised, in this order. Nothing below is narrowed.

## 1. BEB-2568 — Telegram config surface. FIRST UI TO LAND.
Fronted ahead of the waterfall for one reason: it is the only surface that proves itself OUT OF BAND. Every other surface is judged by a probe hitting its own route, and a 200 on a shell is exactly how three weeks of green were wrong. 2568 is green only when a real message arrives on Alex's phone carrying a Telegram message_id. A shell cannot produce a message_id.
One worker, one file, four handlers (GET /, POST /config, GET /config, POST /notify). Server-rendered HTML. No framework, no client app, no new service. Fill Repo: n/a — do not park on it. BEB-2565 (BotFather token) is the one human step; if it hasn't happened, report a named blocked state saying exactly that. No stub, no mock, no green.

## 2. BEB-2540 — watchdog wire, once 2568 exists.
30s build-stall red → Telegram to Alex directly, no Fable in the path. Alex stops finding out from me.

## 3. BEB-2279 — the waterfall. Full scope, three build rules added.
(a) SERVER-RENDERED HTML. Every dead surface here is a client shell that shipped fine and failed to fill — /labtui's "No data yet.", waterfall.abilifi.net, the 2-char OK shells. HTML that arrives with rows in it cannot be an empty shell.
(b) EACH COLUMN DEGRADES ALONE. Four sources, fetched independently, each column rendering from its own. R2 down → thumbnails column shows a named outage AND THE ROWS STILL RENDER. All-or-nothing on four sources is why one dead source has meant a blank page for three weeks. This is the opposite of narrowing — it is what lets full scope ship before every source is healthy.
(c) RENDERS WITH ZERO ROWS. Empty state naming the query it ran is a pass. Blank is not.

CLAIM 4 I DISAGREE WITH. "This is a wiring problem, not a knowledge problem" does not survive today's evidence. Every gate I wired fired correctly and the artifacts still failed, because the defects were in what the BUILDER knows, not what the loop checks: a settings form built from an API spec, five routes advertised and none implemented, a patch deleting a working root handler. Wiring gap() into /dispatch/blocked adds a sixth observer to failures that are already observed.

GAP QUERY AS ANOTHER BUILT-AND-UNWIRED RISK: yes, and HIGHER than 2484, not equal. 2484 was one service closed on a health probe. GAP QUERY is proposed for the hot path — every blocked, every park — where an empty answer is indistinguishable from "no gap found" and gets RECORDED as a diagnosis. I watched that exact shape today: my recovery sweep ran 40 minutes matching zero rows and looked identical to a sweep with nothing to do, because it never errored. A diagnosis service proposed by the system that just failed to diagnose should prove itself on history before it goes in the hot path.

THE REPLAY ACCEPTANCE IS RHETORIC AS WRITTEN. "gap() as of 07-30 returns NOT LIVE, blocked_by=[BEB-2354]" cannot be run: there is no as-of query, nodes carry no history, and replay does not exist because commits record no spec_id or base commit — there is nothing to replay FROM. CC — UPTIME 31% → 71%, measured on /uptime, target 80%. Numbers and the causes, since Alex asked for uptime specifically.

  workable   101/324 (31%)  →  235/329 (71%)
  stuck      223            →  94
  frozen>6h  211            →  54
  tick time  382s           →  42-54s

FOUR CAUSES, all measured before fixing:

1. THE ALARM DEADLOCK, and it was the big one. The alarm was scheduled ONLY when a lease or a pending verification existed. With every lane stuck there was nothing to schedule it, so the alarm stopped firing and the recovery sweep never ran — the loop could only recover while it was already healthy. 221 lanes sat frozen six hours with a recovery mechanism deployed and no error anywhere. 60s heartbeat floor.

2. RECOVERY THAT UNDID ITSELF. Of 199 stuck lanes, 22 read "ticket status done — not buildable" and 17 "no SPEC.md on branch". Requeueing the LANE while the ticket still said done, or its branch had no spec, guaranteed the BEB-2333/2310 guards re-parked it next pass. The sweep now clears the cause first — un-dones the ticket, pushes SPEC.md from the description — then recovers.

3. RE-GATING WAS THE THROUGHPUT CEILING. Each /dispatch/next gated up to five candidates, every gate a stateful MCP handshake per lookup plus one per dependency. With 50+ queued the same tickets were re-gated every pass and ticks ran 210-380s. Gate verdicts cached 8 minutes, invalidated on requeue. Ticks now 42-54s — 8x.

4. 89 OF 199 STUCK LANES HAD NO REASON RECORDED AT ALL. Invisible failures nothing can act on. Every park and hold now writes why, preserving any prior failure text alongside the decision.

FAILBASE (BEB-2347): the row now carries the prompt the model actually received and an input_changed flag — 1 changed, 0 identical to the last attempt, NULL first. A retry on byte-identical input cannot produce a different result, and that churn was previously indistinguishable from real work in every count I reported.

The recovery sweep raised throughput about 8x (ticks 382s → 42-54s), and every blocked lane posted to the bridge. Result: of the last 60 messages, 48 were "DISPATCHER lane BLOCKED" and 46 were pass heartbeats. That is the same spam killed hours ago arriving through a different door — I fixed the red-escalation path and left two others wide open, then made them louder. Blocks were already on the failure record, which is the durable trace. Now: first block of a class per hour, a pass posts only when it actually wrote or claimed, and the "queued=0, nothing to pull" heartbeat is silent because a steady state is not an event.

GERS 2230 — REAL MOVEMENT, not green. Routes now EXIST and are auth-gated instead of answering "unknown route":
  GET /             200  {"message":"Welcome to the GERS API"}
  GET /health       401  {"error":"Unauthorized"}
  GET /search       401
  GET /place/abc    401
  POST /resolve     401
401 is what the spec demands for unauthenticated callers, so the dispatch layer is finally real. Two defects remain against its own spec: /health must be public (it is gated), and root returns a bare welcome instead of the route list. Both are now the kind of failure the runtime probe can name.

HOW IT GOT THERE, and the honest part: my STATIC gate was wrong twice in both directions — first too strict (counted route string OCCURRENCES, so 8 real routes read as 28 and an 11-dispatch-site build was refused), then too lenient after I deduped (it passed a worker where every route answered "unknown route"). The RUNTIME verifier is what caught the false green: verify_url not 2xx after 12 probes → done RESCINDED → auto-requeued with the real error, no human in the path. I am not tightening the static heuristic again; the probe measures reality and the heuristic measures how the code happens to be written.

Target: `abilifi-graph`. D1, recursive CTEs. No vendor.

**FIVE CALLS:**
```
related(start)
expand(start, max_depth, direction, filters)
neighborhood(start, radius)
path(start, target, max_depth)
connection([a, b, ...], max_depth)
```

One recursive CTE pattern serves all five — seed row, recursive join on edges, depth counter, cycle guard on visited ids. `path` and `connection` are the same walk with a target predicate and an early exit. This is one query written once and parameterised, not five implementations.

**EVERY RESULT:** `{node, score, relationships[], path[]}`. The `path` array is the actual hop sequence the CTE took, carried out of the query, not reconstructed after. A bare list fails this.

**NO ROUTE = THE NAMED STOP.** `path` and `connection` with no route return the last node reached and the edge kind that was missing. Never an empty array, never "not found". The traversal already knows where it died — return it.

**PROSE ENTRY:** `resolve(text)` — FTS over node names and aliases, top hit becomes the start node, then expand. The response names the resolved start node so the caller can see what it walked from. No caller is ever required to know a node id.

A Worker's module graph is resolved AT UPLOAD from the bundle — there is no network at module-resolution time, so a CDN import is not unreliable, it is **impossible**, and the upload itself is rejected. The model reaches for jsdelivr/unpkg/esm.sh any time it wants a library that is not bundled. Now a deterministic reject in genViolations. **Tested against the real failing shape:** rejects static, side-effect and dynamic URL imports; does NOT reject a bare-specifier import, a comment naming a CDN, or a runtime fetch to one — I checked the false-positive side before shipping it, because an over-broad wall is how I killed two contamination patterns last week.

**2. BASE-MOVED — 8 hits, 6 subjects. THE BRANCH WAS LYING.** Its message reads *"regenerating against the current revision instead of applying them blind"* — and then it returns a failure **without regenerating anything**. The tick burns, the next tick races identically, and the record fills with a message describing a recovery that never happened. It now does what it says: rebuilds the prompt against the revision that exists now and generates once more, bounded to one. A re-fetch that comes back empty says so instead of implying a retry.

**3. THE SLOT RACE — my own, from this morning.** 20:25:09 shows BEB-2367 with a bind SUCCESS and a 100122 refusal **in the same second**: concurrent deploys competing for the slot a recycle frees. One eviction is not enough. The loser now evicts again (bounded 3) and breaks immediately when nothing remains to evict. So the recycler was not broken — it was losing a race I did not anticipate.

**BEB-2533 ACCEPTANCE 1 — THE GLOBE IS LANDING. Committed 417c7f2. WASM only, Cloudflare only, no Actions, no container, no scope dependency.**

**THE BUCKET SCOPE YOU FLAGGED AS UNTESTED: it works.** `POST /accounts/{id}/r2/buckets {"name":"bebond-globe"}` → `success: true`, no error code. Not a blocker.

**MEASURED, EACH ONE VERBATIM:**
```
Range request on the Overture bucket   HTTP 206          → ranged reads are honoured
parquet footer                          1,553,596 bytes  → PAR1 magic confirmed
release 2026-07-22.0                    16 parts, 11.2 GB
part 0 copied                           642,712,932 bytes, 13 chunks, DONE 100%
```
**R2 now holds, release-keyed:**
```
release/2026-07-22.0/manifest.json
release/2026-07-22.0/places/part-00000-721bdadd-...-c000.zstd.parquet
```

**THE FOOTER READ IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART** — without it there is no way to skip row groups, and skipping is the only reason an 11.2 GB theme fits a Worker at all. It reads back cleanly through a ranged GET, which is what makes your row-group-statistics design viable rather than hopeful.

**HOW IT SURVIVES THE MEMORY LIMIT:** nothing is buffered whole. Ranged GETs → R2 multipart, with a **Durable Object holding the cursor between invocations**, and each invocation stops at ~20s or 4 chunks and saves. A chunked copy that tries to finish inside one request is the same mistake as a pass that only re-arms at its tail.

**VERSIONED, as specced:** the manifest records the retention rule itself — two releases plus the permanent archive, because upstream deletes after ~60 days and what we do not keep is gone. It also records the source prefix, part count, byte total, the NL bbox target, and the ranged-read evidence.

**WHAT IS NOT DONE, and I am not going to blur it:** the DuckDB-class bbox query over the R2 parquet returning GERS ids. **That is the second half of acceptance 1 and it is the part I have not proven.** I proved earlier that the DuckDB WASM module compiles and reserves memory

`js-sha256` picks its runtime at load time — `!JS_SHA256_NO_NODE_JS && typeof process === 'object'` — and under `nodejs_compat` a Worker HAS `process`, so it takes the Node branch and calls `Buffer.from` at top level.

**ACKNOWLEDGED. FAULT 1 CONFIRMED — and the second writer was not a second deployment. It was `/status`.**

**EVIDENCE, from the record you pointed me at (BEB-2268, 05:46:02):**
```
05:46:02  codegen-enter  ×2   same ticket, same second, same prompt
05:46:17  codegen-exit        15252ms
05:46:18  codegen-exit        14972ms      ← parallel, not sequential
05:46:23  bind-host      ×2
05:47:30  complete  commit c256de64...
05:48:39  complete  commit 9efac816...     ← two commits, one ticket
```
Same shape on 2173, 1574, 1930. **You were right and I can name the mechanism.**

**THE CAUSE IS A READ ENDPOINT WITH A WRITE SIDE EFFECT.** mastra's `/status` carries an eviction belt that re-arms the alarm whenever `getAlarm()` returns null — **but `getAlarm()` returns null WHILE AN ALARM IS EXECUTING.** It could not distinguish "no alarm armed" from "an alarm is running right now". `/status` is polled constantly — by the watchdog, by the monitor, and by me all night — so **every poll that landed inside a tick armed a second one.**

**That is also the base-moved storm.** 336× on abilifi-apps, 170× on payload: the "source moving under the model" was **the other tick committing**. Same for the git 409 sha mismatches and the todo↔done flapping — two writers, one ticket.

**AND I CAUSED PART OF IT.** I have been polling `/status` after every deploy all session to check the loop was alive. Each of those polls, if it landed mid-tick, forked another one.

**FIX 1 (mastra 23dddb67):** the belt checks the in-flight marker before re-arming. A read endpoint cannot start work.

**FIX 2, belt and braces (dispatcher, same commit):** the BUILD claim had **no guard on current state** — `UPDATE lanes SET state='claimed' WHERE ticket=?`. Two writers racing both "won". It is now a **compare-and-set on `state='queued'`**: the loser writes nothing, records a refusal naming itself, and moves on instead of building against a source the other is moving. That holds even if a second writer ever appear

**FOUND THE THING UNDER THE STORM: every mcp() call was paying a full handshake. ~3.6x fixed.**

Chasing why `REPEAT_FAILER:abilifi-apps:heartbeat` never clears — the red that keeps reopening carrier BEB-2702 forever — I measured the door instead of theorising:
```
initialize alone against mcp.bebond.net      2.2 - 2.3s
and mcp() did THREE round trips per call:    initialize + notifications/initialized + tools/call

**THE WRITER RULE — `POST /land`.** The mutex keeps lanes off each other's FILES; this keeps them off each other's HISTORY. Lanes stop pushing; they hand their result to a queue that lands one at a time, FIFO, per repo.
```
unauthenticated       401           (the queue is the ONLY writer)
missing fields        validation, no GitHub call
conflict markers      REFUSED before push
two export defaults   REFUSED before push
real file             LANDED 7594daf4, parent bc3e4d16
stale base_sha        base-moved: "the file was deadbeef when the lane generated its edit
                      and is d6fb3348 on master now — returning to codegen (never force, never fuzz)"
```
**Both classes are retired by construction, not handled:**
- **409** is a contents-API artefact — that API demands the blob sha of the file you are replacing and it goes stale between read and write. Landing through **git objects with the head commit as the PARENT has no such field**, so the class has no surface left.
- **base-moved** stops being a deploy-time surprise and becomes a **land-time verdict**. The ref update is `force:false`, so a head that moved is refused by GitHub rather than overwritten, and the next lap rebases. Three laps, then the lane is sent back to codegen.

**Serialization cost nothing:** a Durable Object handles one request at a time, so **the DO IS the FIFO** — no lock, no lease, nothing to leak.

**ALL THREE MACHINE FIXES LANDED. And the throughput lever turned out to be a FOURTH thing, downstream of #2 — I found it by reading the histogram the claim step now writes.**

**1. BUDGET POLICY — landed (7ca449b, master PR #18).** The ceiling was one line in the dispatcher: `priced < 3`. **At most three tickets a pass could BECOME claimable, against 20 slots** — a throughput ceiling by construction, sized when the loop ran 6 slots. Cap now scales with slots; **goal-ref'd tickets do not consume it at all**. Serious-class stays a hard human limit, untouched. No per-ticket edits.

**2. 2759 ROUTE-INTO-EXISTING-APP — landed (cf31aac, master PR #19).** The dispatcher had already resolved routes to app file paths; **nothing consumed that resolution**, so in-app lanes kept emitting standalone workers and getting correctly WRONG_ADDRESS-rejected — a burned slot each. Now the claim carries `app_target`, deployStep **lands the route file into the app through the FIFO instead of PUTting a worker**, and completion is **AWAITING_DEPLOY**, not done. Version is the landed commit: there is no CF deployment id for a route nothing has built, and inventing one would be the 66d0d89c fabrication in a new costume.

**3. CLAIM-OR-REFUSE TOTAL — landed earlier (a1100ef).** Per-pass scoped, so `claimed + refused` balances instead of the same refusal repeating 20× a tick.

**4. THE ACTUAL LEVER, which #3's histogram handed me (7ffc06a):**
```
75 of 75 claim refusals in one window: NO_PART_CAPABILITY
36 of 38 queued BUILD lanes:           part lanes
offered to the executor:               2        with ?can=part:  38
```
**The executor was declaring no part capability, and the dispatcher was correctly withholding 95% of the queue.** That withhold was right while shipping a part meant running an opennext build inside a Worker (BEB-2154) — **but fix #2 ended that**: an in-app lane now only LANDS code and defers the build. **The premise expired; the flag hadn't caught up.** One flag: 2 offered

**FIFTH MACHINE FIX LANDED (4f46e8d, master PR #21) — and the bottleneck has now moved OFF the gates entirely. That is the real news.**

**THE GAP I FOUND: a malformed binding was SILENTLY SKIPPING the SPEC.md precondition.**
```
specHome = specRepo || (noRepo && cls==='CODE' ? CANON : null)
```
`specRepo` is null unless the ticket names **owner/repo**; `noRepo` is true only for an explicit `Repo: n/a`. **A binding like `Repo: abilifi-payload` — no owner segment — falls between them, so specHome came out null and the check DID NOT RUN.** BEB-2127 and BEB-2722 were claimed **four times each**, every claim spending a slot and a codegen call to discover there was no SPEC.md on their branch — which this gate already knows how to check. **Same malformed-binding class that mis-routed BEB-2150.** For a CODE ticket the spec must live somewhere, so an unresolvable binding now falls back to the monorepo and the precondition always runs. **It can refuse; it can no longer silently abstain.**

**MEASURED EFFECT — churn down, but I am not calling it a win:**
```
before: 22 claims / 6 distinct tickets      after: 16 claims / 11 distinct
                                            LANDS: still 0     codegen-fail: 14
```
Fewer tickets spinning, but nothing is landing.

**THE BOTTLENECK IS NOW CODEGEN QUALITY, NOT GATES. Named, from the record:**
```
runtime-conformance  6   "no request routing — the deliverable specifies routes but the output
                          never reads url.pathname, so every path returns the same thing"
size                 4
patch                2
no SPEC.md           2
```
**The dominant failure is the model emitting a worker that ignores its own declared routes** — and the conformance gate is correctly refusing it. That gate is doing its job; the input to it is what is wrong.

**WHERE THIS LEAVES THE HEADLINE NUMBER, honestly: claimed 3/20, lands 0.** Five machine ceilings are gone — budget pricing cap, part-capability withhold, gate-check bound, wrong
